report: The patient's tender enlarging scalp lesion, despite a history of squamous cell carcinomas, is diagnosed as malignant myopericytoma. Histopathology shows concentric perivascular proliferation with hyalinized stroma, cytologic atypia, mitoses, and necrosis, indicating malignancy. Immunohistochemistry reveals SMA-positive perivascular cells and CD31-positive vessels with negative epithelial and melanocytic markers, confirming a vascular/perivascular origin and excluding squamous cell carcinoma, adnexal tumors, benign vascular lesions, and inflammatory conditions. Expert pathologic analysis identifies malignant myopericytoma as the most likely diagnosis. Complete excision and follow-up are recommended.
